title: Whole-system Frobenius exchange inverses and integral realization
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and supply a compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $f=pj:X\to Y$ for its base change to $k$ and $g_W$ for geometric Frobenius on $W=X,\overline X,Y$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the category $\mathscr S_W$ of strict semilinear $B_{W,n}$-module systems and its ordinary unbounded derived category, exact evaluations $e_n$, system inverse image $\mathcal G_W$ along $g_W$, derived system direct image $\mathcal F_f$, and exact open extension $\mathcal J_j$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For EVERY $C\in D(\mathscr S_X)$, let
$$e_{f,C}:\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_fC\longrightarrow\mathcal F_f\mathcal G_XC,$$
$$e^c_{f,C}:\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_p\mathcal J_jC\longrightarrow\mathcal F_p\mathcal J_j\mathcal G_XC$$
be the actual system mate and proper/open composite of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], formed before evaluation, with $C$ in place of the reduction system there. Both maps are isomorphisms in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$, natural in $C$. Their inverse system morphisms evaluate at $n$ to the inverses of the specified finite direct and chosen compact exchanges on $e_nC$, through the evaluated adjunction and operation comparisons. This is an assertion about whole system morphisms; no faithfulness of evaluation on morphisms is assumed. No boundedness, constructibility, normalization, or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $C$ is imposed.

For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $\mathcal R_XK$ be simultaneous derived reduction with quotient-induced transitions, $U_Y$ exact scalar restriction to $\widehat R_Y$-module towers, and $\mathcal L_Y=R\lim U_Y$ with the strict-tower derived-limit functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Use exactly the natural operation comparisons $\alpha_*,\beta_*,\alpha_!,\beta_!$ of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. The specified integral exchanges $\beta_*\mathcal L_Y(e_f)\alpha_*$ and $\beta_!\mathcal L_Y(e_f^c)\alpha_!$ are invertible, with inverses respectively
$$\alpha_*^{-1}\mathcal L_Y(e_f^{-1})\beta_*^{-1},\qquad\alpha_!^{-1}\mathcal L_Y((e_f^c)^{-1})\beta_!^{-1},$$
where the system maps are evaluated at $\mathcal R_XK$. The same fixed compactification is used at every level. The conclusion refers to the specified whole-system maps and their realization, rather than to any choice of an integral arrow with those individual finite reductions.

proof.text: For whole-system invertibility there is a shorter route than finite evaluation. The canonical system pullback compositor and identity comparison give inverse functors for pullback along any scheme isomorphism. Apply isIso_mateEquiv_of_isEquivalence_of_fullyFaithful to the specified systemSquare and systemAdjunction: the actual direct exchange is invertible. Repeat for the proper part of the retained compactification. The open system exchange is already a natural isomorphism, so whiskering and composition prove invertibility of the actual compact system exchange. The remaining evaluation and integral inverse assertions follow the existing steps below.

For direct evaluation, apply systemExchange_evaluation from def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization. Conjugate the evaluated system isomorphism by exactly systemPullEvaluation, systemDirectEvaluation and openSquareDerivedPullbackModel in the stated source and target coordinates. Cancel the pullback-model comparisons: the hom is finiteTensorExchange. The inverse of this explicitly constructed composite is target.inv followed by evaluation of the system inverse followed by source.hom. This gives the direct inverse-evaluation clause without faithfulness or joint conservativity. The compact inverse-evaluation clause remains to be formalized: evaluate the specified proper/open composite using the same retained compactification and operation comparisons, then use the same inverse-of-a-composite calculation.

proof.text: For either exchange write $e:A\Rightarrow B$. Define $v_C=e_C^{-1}$ in the system derived category, so $v_Ce_C=1$ and $e_Cv_C=1$. From $B(h)e_C=e_DA(h)$, cancellation gives $A(h)v_C=v_DB(h)$; hence the inverses are natural. Applying the evaluation functor [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to both inverse identities shows that $e_n(v_C)$ is the inverse of $e_n(e_C)$. Conjugate by exactly the operation comparisons used in step 1. Uniqueness of an inverse identifies the resulting arrow with the inverse of the specified finite direct or compact exchange. No equality of arbitrary system morphisms is inferred from evaluation.

proof.text: For $C=\mathcal R_XK$, [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and the exact scalar restriction in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] give the functor $\mathcal L_Y=R\lim U_Y$. It sends $ve=1$ and $ev=1$ to the same identities for $\mathcal L_Y(v),\mathcal L_Y(e)$. For either sign, put $t=\beta\mathcal L_Y(e)\alpha$, the specified integral arrow of that definition. Set $s=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal L_Y(v)\beta^{-1}$. Associativity, the inverse identities for $\alpha,\beta$, and the two functorial identities give $st=1$ and $ts=1$. Substituting $e=e_f$ and $e=e_f^c$ gives exactly the two claimed inverses. The comparisons are natural isomorphisms on the stated bounded integral domain; the argument uses their specified arrows and the fixed $c$, without selecting an arrow by its finite reductions.

split_report.summary: No statement change and no new nodes. Evaluated the actual system mates using the existing semilinear derived calculus, applied the existing ambient finite exchange inverse lemma, and used joint conservativity solely to detect invertibility. Evaluating inverse identities and applying the strict-tower derived-limit functor proves the precise inverse formulas. Checked unbounded, noncartesian inputs and fixed-compactification hypotheses.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the integral whole-system part of the first isomorphism in both ordinary and compact-support composites of def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius, through lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso; precisely the inherited from.place (returned step 7 before rational localization).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q104-11050e130 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Stage-1 split of Q78's node C. There are no new nodes. The statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are byte-identical to the Q78 snapshot; only the proof fields, split_report and the added searches change. No SGA source is cited: Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.14), printed pp. 150-153, checked in the PDF; proof_origin agent is correct. Step 1: lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections gives evaluation compatibility for pullback (u = g_W, constant A_n), system direct image, J_j, units, counits and mates, so e_n(e_{f,C}) is FrEx_{f,*}(e_nC) and e_n(e^c) is Rp_*(b)∘FrEx_{p,*}(j_!e_nC), up to comparisons. lem-weil-frobenius-finite-exchange-inverse covers every unbounded K in D(X_proet,A_n), the same f_0 hypotheses (no separatedness of X_0, Y_0) and a fixed c. Its etale-origin clause is not used. It is true because the g's are scheme isomorphisms. Step 2: joint detection of isomorphisms is a stated clause of lem-coef and holds because exactness is componentwise; naturality comes from the def. Steps 3-4 are elementary: inverses are unique, and L_Y = R lim U_Y is a functor (prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality). This gives (α⁻¹L(v)β⁻¹)(βL(e)α) = 1 both ways. Edge cases checked: C = 0, unbounded or non-normalized C, f_0 = id, empty X, n = 1. Duplicate search: lem-coef-frobenius-exchange-equivalence (rational, compact support, separated schemes) and the system-realization/descent defs differ; no node states the whole-system inverse. Tool uses accepted: prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality (declared) and lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections (undeclared, but it is the stmt_dep calculus of the item and of def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange, and no unit node gives it). review_split 'no such node' lines are a symlink artifact; every cited node exists.
